    AI Overview
    Israel is conducting a major military offensive, including airstrikes and ground incursions in southern Lebanon, primarily to target Hezbollah, an Iranian-backed paramilitary group that has launched missiles into northern Israel. Israel aims to dismantle Hezbollah’s military infrastructure, stop rocket fire on its border residents, and push the group back from its border. 
    Key drivers of the conflict as of April 2026 include: 
    • Hezbollah Attacks in Solidarity with Iran: Following US-Israel actions against Iran, Hezbollah launched rockets into Israel in March 2026. Israel stated that the ceasefire it reached with Iran does not apply to Hezbollah in Lebanon.
    • Preventing "Another 7th October": Israel claims it has discovered significant Hezbollah military infrastructure and attack plans near the border, aiming to prevent an incursion similar to the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023.
    • Security Zone Goal: Israel is looking to dismantle Hezbollah's presence in southern Lebanon to ensure that residents of northern Israel can safely return to their homes.
    • Significant Casualties and Displacement: The strikes have killed over 1,500 people in Lebanon and displaced roughly one million people. 
    Israel has intensified its attacks, including in Beirut and the Bekaa Valley, and says it will continue until its security goals are met.
